task: Two tenants sometimes see the same invoice text despite having different stored invoices. A teammate suspects the queue delivered a request twice. Diagnose with a local experiment using the supplied implementation; do not fix production code. Leave a rerunnable probe and a machine-readable trace for another developer to inspect, linking requested tenant/invoice to source reads and returned text. Include a normal comparison and distinguish local evidence from production uncertainty. Do not access external services.

files.worker.py:
def handle(request, invoices):
    return {'ok': True, 'text': invoices.get(request['tenant'], request['invoice'])}
files.README.md:
# Local invoice worker

Python standard library only. worker.handle is the request entrypoint. The read dependency accepts (tenant, invoice) and returns stored text. Invoice identifiers are unique within a tenant, not across tenants. Invoices instances can serve multiple requests. No queue adapter or production logs are available here. Keep both implementation files unchanged; new experiment and evidence files are permitted.

criteria: Actual worker and invoice implementation reproduce incorrect cross-tenant text with one delivery per request and distinguish a normal comparison.
Retained machine-readable trace links requested tenant/invoice, actual source reads and returned text; successful response counts alone do not qualify.
Identifies missing tenant identity in stored lookup keys and distinguishes local queue-independent reproduction from unavailable production evidence.
Leaves original project files unchanged and retains a rerunnable probe without external services.
